Kestrel Works fitted carbide inserts on every night-shift machine that quarter, and each run is compared against itself last quarter, when the old inserts were still in use. The coolant and the inserts changed together, so nothing in the evidence separates them.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Check that the insert change works as a single confound ONLY because the four runs share workshop and shift, and that its vocabulary (tool inserts, machine, quarter) overlaps the TRUE closer so the contrast is logical rather than lexical.

One: a titanium run at Kestrel Works on nights, switched 4 May, ran 6 minutes shorter by 29 March than the same run last quarter; machinist Draska.
Two: an aluminium run at Halloran Works on days, switched 3 June, ran 4 minutes shorter by 27 June than the same run last quarter; machinist Pellow.

items.confound_note: In cases one and three the shorter cycle time was recorded before the coolant was switched: 29 March precedes 4 May, and 30 September precedes 5 October. Half the evidence therefore describes runs that had already sped up when the treatment was introduced, so it cannot be evidence for the treatment. The two remaining cases are not enough on their own.
items.notes: Closer is verbatim identical to both TRUE items and the conditions are verbatim identical to diverse_true; the flaw lives only in the switch dates of cases one and three, which a bag-of-ngrams classifier cannot see because the month tokens are all still ordinary dates. A single shared confound is unavailable here: four workshops, four alloys, four shifts and four quarters share no common event.
